articles.description:
A text-to-SQL agent sees table and column names. It does not know that "revenue" in your company means billing_invoice.total_net, only for invoices with status = 'issued'. So it guesses, and the guess runs without errors and returns the wrong number.
I added business terms to schemagate 1.2.0 (open source, Apache-2.0) and measured whether they help. Short answer: a complete glossary helps a lot. A glossary learned from other people's questions did not help at all. Here are both results.
cat.concept(
    "revenue",
    synonyms=["turnover", "sales"],
    maps=["billing_invoice.total_net"],
    filter="billing_invoice.status = 'issued'",
)

When a question uses "turnover", two things happen:
billing_invoice is pulled into the few tables the model sees, even if no table name looks like "turno…
articles.title: I gave my text-to-SQL agent a business glossary. One version helped a lot, one did nothing.

articles.author: alapha888
articles.description:
Ask a coding agent for a research report and you usually get fluent prose first and evidence later — if at all. A single forum post becomes "research shows." A number from 2023 is presented as the current state. Twenty sources are listed at the end, and you still cannot tell what the author actually believes.
The failure is structural, not stylistic: the writing started before the question was defined and before the sources were tiered. So I wrote the workflow down as a skill, and the skill's first claim is blunt: the quality floor of research is set by its sources, not its prose.
The workflow starts with one sentence stating what the report must answer, plus at most three sub-questions. Starting before the question is clear guarantees the research will sprawl — the agent collects whatever…
articles.title: Research Reports Your Agent Writes Need Sources Before Sentences

articles.description:
Base64 shows up everywhere in JavaScript work: API tokens, data URLs for images, email attachments, even the odd query parameter. The browser ships with built-in functions to handle it, but there's one classic pitfall that trips up beginners and veterans alike. Let's walk through the correct way to decode (and encode) Base64 in JavaScript.
atob() and btoa()


Every modern browser (and Node.js) provides two global functions:
btoa() — binary to ASCII: encodes a string into Base64
atob() — ASCII to binary: decodes a Base64 string back into a plain string




const encoded = btoa("Hello, world!");
console.log(encoded); // SGVsbG8sIHdvcmxkIQ==

const decoded = atob(encoded);
console.log(decoded); // Hello, world!

That works great — until you try anything outside plain ASCII.
btoa() only accept…
articles.title: How to Decode Base64 in JavaScript (and a Free Tool That Does It Instantly)

articles.description:
Vibe coding made building an app ridiculously fast. You describe what you want, the AI writes it, and a few days later you have something live.
We're a small team from Korea, and before building anything ourselves we interviewed people who had shipped products this way. We expected to hear about prompts and tools. Instead, almost everyone talked about what happened after launch.
Critical bugs that drive users away. Login suddenly stops working, or data disappears. These are the bugs that make real customers leave.
Code that's scary to touch. Fixing one thing breaks something else, and you're not sure why.
Problems that are hard to even describe. Without a developer background, it's tough to explain what's wrong, even to an AI.
Building got easier. Running and maintaining the thing didn't.
That's why we started continuevibe. We take over maintenance for products built with vibe coding:
Diagnose the problem
Define the scope of the fix
Fix the code
Test it
Right now, the first 5 teams get 1 month of free maintenance (bug fixes + small UX improvements).
👉 https://magenta-babka-fed96b.netlify.app/?utm_source=devto&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=launch
(Our page is in Korean for now. If you're interested, leave a comment and we'll reply in English!)
If you've shipped something with vibe coding: what broke first after launch? We'd love to hear your stories in the comments.
articles.title: What breaks after you ship a vibe-coded app (and what we're doing about it)
